body.estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\theta_b(P_O)\text{ for }P\in\mathcal M_b,\ b\in\{\mathrm{PT},\mathrm{SC}\};\quad \phi_U(P_0)=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\}\), where the centered coefficients solve \(\mathrm{QP}_x\).

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed-length micro panel with finite group and covariate supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Group one is untreated through \(T-1\) and treated only in period \(T\); every donor group remains untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \((G,X)\) cell has probability bounded away from zero by the displayed margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The treated-stratum probabilities \(\nu_x\), conditional contrasts \(C_b(x)\), centered contrast gradients \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\), normalized restriction gradients, and covariance Grams are finite-dimensional observed-law objects for the lower-bound and adaptation calculations. The branch-chart extension includes the branch-specific \(\chi_b(P)\) off the intersection. No cross-fitted projection estimator, variance estimator, data-driven chart coupling, or multiplier procedure is proved valid over the frozen local-sequence class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. The SC identification condition uses covariate-indexed weights shared across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); its regular SC estimation theorem uses a nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent to full column rank of augmented \(B\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Corrected union-envelope theorem and uniform-attainment obstruction

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives covariance-optimal PT weighting but no PT-or-SC affine intersection, treated-composition decomposition, or union lower bound.
Section 3 studies local efficiency for a different finite-support union model, not the PT--SC ATT tangent geometry here.
Proposition 1(a), equations (2.11)--(2.12), give the two-group panel-DiD ATT efficient influence function and bound, including the treated-composition component.
Its cross-fit remainder theory is guidance for a repaired theorem with common rate control; it does not validate finite-coordinate-spliced sequence uniformity.
Its branchwise-drift analysis is guidance for a repaired theorem but does not remove the frozen class's finite-coordinate-splicing obstruction.
Its multiplier coupling theory is guidance only after a genuinely uniform influence expansion is available.

body.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. The corrected pathwise derivative separates the treated-composition gradient \(\chi_b\) from conditionally centered contrast gradients \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\). At intersection laws, the two conditional contrasts and composition gradients agree, so the common term is orthogonal to the centered PT and SC faces and the efficiency envelope still reduces to finite covariance-weighted programs, with \(E[\chi_0^2]\) added to the envelope and both oracle variances. Observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided adaptation. The exact three-group constants and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoints are unchanged. The result is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark only: finite-coordinate splicing makes the requested uniformly chartwise one-step, variance, and multiplier theorem false over the frozen sequence class.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under PT or SC and gives distinct branchwise influence and bootstrap laws; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives PT efficiency alone. Neither source decomposes the branch derivative into its treated-composition and centered conditional-contrast components or determines the regular influence intersection and convolution bound for the nonnested union.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support turns each branch into finitely many conditional-mean restrictions. Separating \(\chi_b\) from \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\) restores the product rule; at an intersection, the common \(\chi_0\) is orthogonal to the centered restriction geometry, so the efficiency loss and adaptation frontier remain computable from observed conditional covariance Grams.
project_justification.fill: The project derives corrected PT and SC affine influence classes, including the treated-composition gradient, solves their centered intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, and adds \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to the union and oracle variances. It proves simultaneous and one-sided oracle criteria, the strict three-group region, and both endpoint reductions. The envelope is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark, not an implemented standard error. The frozen sequence class cannot support the requested uniform one-step and multiplier theorem because it permits arbitrary finite-coordinate splicing.

body.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor. Its PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem need not identify weights uniquely, while its regular SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent, after reparameterization, to full column rank of augmented \(B\). The present model is a finite-support, uniform-overlap, uniform-moment, full-rank subclass. The corrected derivative explicitly adds the treated-composition term that is present in branchwise ATT influence laws. SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, remain branchwise results; this paper adds a sharp local union-regular lower-bound benchmark and no implemented inference. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting but not the nonnested union geometry. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different union model. SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equations (2.11)--(2.12), supplies the panel-DiD gradient and bound recovered when \(J=1\). Newey1990, Sections 2--3, supplies the generic regular-estimator efficiency lower bound, while Newey1994 is retained only for its separate constant-rank role. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance for a possible repaired uniform theorem. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer by restriction to estimators regular over the broader published union, while sharpness is local to the stated subclass. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 motivate the benchmark but receive no new standard-error procedure here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected union envelope is a local regularity lower bound at fixed-rank intersection laws. Its common treated-composition component is analytically identified, but no attaining estimator, usable standard error, or multiplier-confidence procedure is established. The negative theorem depends on the frozen sequence class's closure under arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements and does not settle a redesigned common neighborhood with common QMD, score, and remainder bounds. Rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing support, covariance degeneracy, and weight-boundary restrictions require different local experiments.
body.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are the corrected tangent-normal characterization \(\mathcal I_b=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}R_b\), the finite centered union convolution lower bound with the additional term \(E[\chi_0^2]\), observable oracle-adaptation tests, the unchanged exact three-group witness, and the single-donor and saturated-donor reductions. The bound is sharp only in the stated local tangent experiment and supplies a benchmark, not implemented inference. The frozen local-sequence class makes a single uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and hence the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage theorem, false by finite-coordinate splicing. No positive sequencewise continuation theorem is claimed.
